home.heroLead:
The deep flavor of carefully selected Kuroge Wagyu, vibrant dishes that reflect the four seasons, and a refined Japanese setting.
With a uniquely Japanese sense of beauty and heartfelt hospitality, we turn your time with someone special into a memory you will never forget.
home.introTitle: From choosing the beef to the last slice
introBody: At Sakura, Omi beef and Japanese Kuroge Wagyu are served in two broths: our signature Kiwami broth and a sukiyaki-style broth.
Along with spacious table seating, we have horigotatsu rooms that work well for families with children. No experience needed. Just come hungry.
home.stylesLead: Our course lets you try both, with two different broths at your table.

sukiyaki.name: Sukiyaki
sukiyaki.body: Beef simmered in our sweet-savory sukiyaki-style broth, bringing out the sweetness of Wagyu fat.

shabushabu.name: Shabu-shabu
shabushabu.body: Swished for a few seconds through our Kiwami broth, so you taste the beef itself: its aroma and tenderness.

home.firstBody: Why raw egg? How long do you swish the beef? Our step-by-step guide has you covered.

groups.standard: Try shabu-shabu and sukiyaki side by side in two broths. Choose by type of meat.

guide.title: How to eat
guide.lead: Our staff will help you at the table, so there is nothing to memorize. Knowing the flow just makes it more fun.

sukiyakiSteps.title: Beat the egg
sukiyakiSteps.body: Lightly beat the raw egg in your small bowl. Dipping the hot beef cools it slightly and makes it silky. Eggs in Japan are produced to be eaten raw.

sukiyakiSteps.title: Simmer the beef
sukiyakiSteps.body: Add a slice to the sukiyaki-style broth. It is ready as soon as the color changes.

sukiyakiSteps.title: Beef first, then vegetables
sukiyakiSteps.body: Simmer vegetables and tofu in the sauce once it has taken on the flavor of the beef.

sukiyakiSteps.title: Finish
sukiyakiSteps.body: End with udon noodles or rice porridge.

shabuSteps.title: Heat the broth
shabuSteps.body: When the Kiwami broth is at a gentle simmer, you are ready.

shabuSteps.title: Swish a few times
shabuSteps.body: Hold one slice with chopsticks and swish it through the broth 2–3 times. It is ready when a little pink remains.

shabuSteps.title: Dip in sauce
shabuSteps.body: Rich sesame sauce or light citrus ponzu. Try both.

shabuSteps.title: Finish with porridge or udon
shabuSteps.body: We use the flavorful broth to make rice porridge or udon noodles.

guide.eggTitle: Prefer not to eat raw egg?
guide.eggBody: We can serve a soft-boiled egg, or sukiyaki without egg. Just ask.

items.a: We recommend booking, as seating is limited. Walk-ins are welcome when tables are available.
In most cases we can offer alternatives for egg, wheat, sesame and more. Please tell us when you book.

items.q: Do you offer vegetarian or halal options?
items.a: We can prepare a vegetable-based course with 2 days' notice. We are not halal certified.

Yes. Add ¥3,000 to the Omi beef & Kuroge Wagyu course or the Kuroge Wagyu course, ¥4,500 to the Omi beef course, or ¥2,000 to the Hida pork course to make it all-you-can-eat. We also offer all-you-can-eat courses: Hida pork for ¥6,480, Kuroge Wagyu for ¥8,980, and Omi beef & Kuroge Wagyu for ¥13,980.
Yes, children of all ages are welcome, including infants. Please let us know when you book.

items.q: Which payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), PayPay and Alipay. IC transit cards and other e-money are not accepted.

items.q: Do you have an English menu?
items.a: Yes, we have an English menu.
We have no parking of our own. There are coin-operated car parks nearby, and we are a short walk from Nagoya Station.
Same-day cancellations and no-shows are charged 100% of the course price.
